verdict.rationale: Vue's official SSR API reference documents first-party streaming renderers in vue/server-renderer for Node streams and Web Streams, so server HTML can be sent progressively. The lazy hydration strategies added in 3.5 let that content display before client code hydrates it. A 2017 community comment naming streaming SSR as a React advantage is old general preference, not a concrete failure, so it does not create a dispute. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of perceived-load gains, and documented out-of-order streaming of async boundaries (Suspense is still experimental).

support.subject: As a developer, I can stream server-rendered content so pages get faster perceived loads before all client code arrives

citations.quote: It is also possible to stream rendering using the Node.js Stream API or Web Streams API.
renderToNodeStream() "Renders input as a Node.js Readable stream"
In Vue 3.5+, async components can control when they are hydrated by providing a hydration strategy.
